data.title: Forbes Books - How to Write and Publish a Book
data.speaker: Joe Gregory, the Authority Company, part of Forbes Books
data.description:
Most founders know a book would help them. Almost none know what the process costs in time, money or attention, so it stays on the list for years.

Joe Gregory has built the publishing arm behind Forbes Books and has taken hundreds of founders from “I should write something” to a printed book. He walks through the whole route: choosing the idea that is worth 200 pages, the ghostwriting and hybrid models and what each really costs, the timeline from first outline to print, and the distribution that decides whether anyone reads it.

Bring a rough idea. You will leave knowing whether it is a book, an article, or nothing.
data.summary: How a book becomes the asset that opens doors — and what it actually takes to publish one.
highlights: Which ideas carry a book and which do not
Ghostwriting, hybrid and self-publishing — real costs and timelines
What publication actually does for inbound and speaking
The first three steps to take this month
data.who_for: Founders considering a book, and anyone already stuck mid-draft.
data.speaker_title: Founder, The Authority Company, Forbes Books
data.speaker_bio: Joe Gregory has spent two decades in business publishing and leads the Forbes Books partner programme in Europe.

data.title: Legal & Tax Risks for Ukrainian Founders abroad
data.speaker: Illya Sverdlov, Imagive Lawyers, parner
data.description:
Moving yourself is simple. Moving a company, or leaving one behind, is not.

Illya Sverdlov works with Ukrainian founders who now live in one country, employ people in a second and invoice from a third. He covers the questions that decide the tax bill: where you are actually resident, when a foreign team creates a permanent establishment, how CFC rules bite, and what a holding structure does and does not solve.

Real cases, and the mistakes that were expensive to unwind.
data.summary: Residency, permanent establishment and the tax traps that catch founders who moved.
highlights: Tax residency: the tests that actually apply, not the 183-day myth
When your team abroad creates a taxable presence
CFC rules for Ukrainian owners
Structures that hold up, and structures that only look tidy
data.who_for: Founders who have relocated, are about to, or run a distributed team.
data.speaker_bio: International tax counsel to founders across the EU, UK and UAE.

data.title: Experience Share event with Forbes Ukraine Entrepreneur 2025
data.speaker: Vitaliy Diatlenko, UKLON
data.description:
An unvarnished experience share. Vitaliy Diatlenko has run UKLON through blackouts, mobilisation and a collapsed unit economy, and rebuilt it into a business that grew through all of it.

No slides about resilience. What broke, what he tried, what he would not do again, and the numbers behind each call. Members ask anything for the last half hour.
data.summary: Scaling a marketplace through a war economy — the decisions, in the founder’s own words.
highlights: Holding a team together when half of it is being mobilised
Pricing and unit economics under permanent uncertainty
What he cut first, and what he protected
Open Q&A — members only
data.who_for: Any member scaling through disruption. Especially useful for marketplaces.
data.speaker_bio: Forbes Ukraine Entrepreneur of the Year 2025.

data.title: Experience Share event with Forbes Ukraine Entrepreneur 2025
data.speaker: Polina Kosharna, SUZIRIA
data.description:
Polina Kosharna built SUZIRIA into a brand people seek out rather than settle for. She takes apart how it happened: the positioning bet, the years before it paid, and the operational grind behind a brand that looks effortless.

Candid on margins, on the hires that mattered, and on the point where she nearly stopped.
data.summary: Building a consumer brand that people choose on purpose — and what it costs.
highlights: Positioning as a decision, not a slogan
What brand actually costs in a small market
The hires that changed the trajectory
Open Q&A — members only
data.who_for: Consumer founders, and anyone whose product is becoming a commodity.
data.speaker_bio: Forbes Ukraine Entrepreneur of the Year 2025.

data.title: Forum Test Drive
data.description:
Forum is the part of EO members talk about years later, and it is almost impossible to explain. So this is not an explanation.

You sit in a facilitated session run exactly as a forum runs: the protocol, the 5%/95% rule, experience shared rather than advice given, and total confidentiality. Eight people, ninety minutes, one real issue each.

Open to members and to prospective members you bring.
data.summary: Ninety minutes inside a real EO forum — the format, not a description of it.
highlights: The forum protocol, run properly
Experience-sharing instead of advice — and why the difference matters
What confidentiality actually means in practice
Whether forum is for you, answered by doing it
data.who_for: New members, and prospective members you would like to introduce.

data.title: Resilience Tour
data.description:
A chapter tour built around one question: what does a company do when the ground moves under it?

Five days across Kyiv and Lviv visiting members’ businesses — manufacturing, logistics, retail, tech — with the founders walking you through what they changed and what it cost. Evenings are for the conversations that only happen in person.

Numbers are limited by the site visits.
data.summary: Five days, two cities, and the businesses that kept going. Kyiv and Lviv, on the ground.
highlights: Site visits hosted by the founders themselves
Kyiv and Lviv, five days, transfers included
Evening dinners with the local chapter
Guests welcome — bring a prospective member
data.who_for: Members from any chapter. Especially those weighing operations in Ukraine.

data.title: European Leadership Conference (ELC) 2026 - Krakow, Poland
data.description:
ELC is where the people who run EO in Europe compare notes. Chapter presidents, learning chairs, membership chairs and staff, in one room for three days.

Track-based: leadership development, chapter operations, and the regional strategy for the year ahead. Immediately before EO Unlimited, so most attendees stay for both.
data.summary: Europe’s chapter leadership, together for three days in Kraków.
highlights: Tracks for presidents, learning, membership and staff
Regional strategy for the year ahead
Runs directly into EO Unlimited — one trip, two events
Kraków old town, three days
data.who_for: Chapter board members and chapter staff.

data.title: EO Unlimited - Krakow, Poland
data.description:
EO Unlimited 2026 Kraków isn’t another business conference — it’s a turning point. For three days, 300 of the world’s most visionary entrepreneurs gather in one of Europe’s most iconic cities to rethink, reshape and lead transformation.

What the three days look like

  • Main-stage speakers, each one a founder who has done the thing they are talking about
  • Deep-dive sessions chosen by the attendees, not by a programme committee
  • The unstructured time that is the real reason people come

The partner programme runs alongside the whole event. Full agenda on the EO Unlimited site.

This div, its style and its onclick are stripped; these words survive.
data.summary: Three days, 300 founders, one of Europe’s most beautiful cities.
highlights: 300 founders from across the EO network
Main stage plus attendee-chosen deep dives
Partner programme throughout
Kraków, four days, October
data.who_for: All EO members. Bring your partner.

data.title: Chapter Retreat
data.description:
The chapter retreat is deliberately unlike every other event: no stage, no agenda imposed from outside, and enough time for conversations to get past the first layer.

Six days in Malta. Mornings are structured — member-led sessions and forum work. Afternoons and evenings are not. Partners are welcome and most members bring them.
data.summary: Six days in Malta with the chapter — the one that sets the tone for the year.
highlights: Member-led sessions each morning
Forum work with your own group
Partners welcome
Six days, single hotel, everything within walking distance

data.title: EMEA Moderator Summit
data.description:
The EMEA Moderator Summit is the annual leadership and training event for forum moderators, run with the Europe and MEPA regions.

Two days of moderator craft: handling the difficult session, keeping the protocol when a group drifts, and the practice that separates a forum that lasts from one that fades.
data.summary: Annual training for forum moderators across Europe, the Middle East, Pakistan and Africa.
highlights: Moderator training, run by experienced moderators
Handling the sessions nobody wants to moderate
Marrakech, two days
Certification counts toward moderator renewal
